problem.title: Problem 10.2: no four mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension six
problem.informal_statement: Decide the frozen universal statement that no four mutually unbiased bases exist in C^6: for every four orthonormal bases of C^6, some pair among them is not mutually unbiased. Unbiasedness is exact equality of every cross squared inner product with 1/6. All arithmetic is exact over the cyclotomic field Q(zeta_12); the factor 1/6 is carried as a rational scalar so that no square root enters the arithmetic. Both a proof and an explicit quadruple are acceptable outcomes. The equivalence group of global unitaries, per-basis reordering, and per-vector phases is used only to normalize the search and is not part of the frozen statement. One retained exact derivation already bounds the problem from below: the pair consisting of the standard basis and the sixth-order discrete Fourier basis extends to a triple, so at least three mutually unbiased bases exist in C^6 and the route through pairwise unextendibility of every pair is refuted. Unextendibility of any single pair excludes only the quadruples containing that pair and never resolves the frozen statement, and exhausting any root-of-unity envelope answers only a restricted sub-question.

target_claim.statement: For every four orthonormal bases B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4 of C^6 there exist indices i and j with i != j such that B_i and B_j are not mutually unbiased, where two orthonormal bases (x_0,...,x_5) and (y_0,...,y_5) of C^6 are mutually unbiased iff the squared modulus of the inner product of x_a with y_b equals exactly 1/6 for all 0 <= a,b <= 5. Equivalently, there exists no set of four pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^6.

assumption_claims.statement: The dimension is exactly 6 and the space is C^6 with the standard Hermitian inner product. An orthonormal basis is a sequence of six pairwise orthogonal unit vectors. Two orthonormal bases (x_0,...,x_5) and (y_0,...,y_5) are mutually unbiased iff for every pair of indices a,b in {0,...,5} the squared modulus of the inner product of x_a with y_b equals exactly 1/6; all 36 conditions are required and none is omitted. Approximate, tolerance-based, or partial unbiasedness on a subset of index pairs is a rejected reading, as is a different constant.

A set of four mutually unbiased bases means four orthonormal bases that are PAIRWISE mutually unbiased, so all six pairs must satisfy all 36 conditions each. Rejected readings: a star configuration in which three bases are each unbiased to one fixed basis but not to one another; an ordered quadruple, which would inflate solution counts; a complete set of seven bases, which is the maximal-set question rather than the frozen one; four bases unbiased in some approximate or averaged sense.

The frozen coefficient field is the cyclotomic field Q(zeta_12), of degree 4 over Q with minimal polynomial Phi_12(x) = x^4 - x^2 + 1, containing zeta_6 = zeta_12^2, the imaginary unit i = zeta_12^3, and sqrt(3) = zeta_12 + zeta_12^(-1). Elements are integer or rational coefficient vectors in the basis (1, zeta_12, zeta_12^2, zeta_12^3) reduced by Phi_12. A basis presented by a matrix of unit-modulus entries carries its normalization as the exact rational scalar 1/6 rather than an entrywise factor 1/sqrt(6), so sqrt(6) is never represented and never enters any coefficient field. The entries of an unknown basis are not restricted to Q(zeta_12): they range over all of C, and the field constrains only the equations and the certificates.

The equivalence group is generated by one global unitary applied simultaneously to all bases, independent reordering of the six vectors within each basis, and independent multiplication of individual basis vectors by unit-modulus scalars. It preserves pairwise unbiasedness, so a quadruple exists if and only if a quadruple with the first basis equal to the standard basis exists, and each remaining basis may be taken in dephased form. The group is used ONLY to normalize the search, and is deliberately NOT part of the frozen statement, which is a universal nonexistence and needs no quotient. Entrywise complex conjugation and permutation of the roles of the bases are excluded from the group; including either changes counts of inequivalent solutions but not the yes-or-no answer, so the exclusion must be stated wherever a count is reported.

Bounded searches in this target restrict the entries of a dephased complex Hadamard matrix to mu_12, the group of twelfth roots of unity, with a declared optional widening to mu_24. This is a strict restriction and not the frozen target. Exhausting the envelope answers only the restricted sub-question, and no report may present envelope exhaustion as an answer to the frozen statement or as unextendibility over C.

For dimension d, the bases given by the columns of the identity and of (1/sqrt(d))*H_1, ..., (1/sqrt(d))*H_r are pairwise mutually unbiased if and only if every H_t is a complex Hadamard matrix, meaning all entries have modulus 1 and the conjugate transpose times the matrix is d times the identity, and (1/sqrt(d))*(conjugate transpose of H_s)*H_t is a complex Hadamard matrix for every s != t.

Two standard facts. First, for coprime positive integers m and n the discrete Fourier matrix of Z_(m*n) equals P*(F_m tensor F_n)*Q for permutation matrices P and Q given by the Chinese Remainder Theorem bijection between Z_(m*n) and Z_m times Z_n; in idempotent form for m = 2, n = 3 the index map j = 3*j_2 + 4*j_3 mod 6 gives j*k = 3*j_2*k_2 + 4*j_3*k_3 mod 6, because the cross terms carry the factor 12 which vanishes mod 6. Second, if A_1,...,A_r are pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^a and B_1,...,B_r are pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^b, then the bases whose vectors are the tensor products of the vectors of A_t with the vectors of B_t, for t = 1,...,r, are pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^(a*b).

A matrix with all entries nonzero has a unique dephasing: unique diagonal matrices D_1, D_2 with the first entry of D_1 equal to 1 such that D_1*M*D_2 has first row and first column all ones. Consequently two dephased matrices H and H' with all entries of modulus 1 satisfy H' = D_1*P_1*H*P_2*D_2 for some diagonal unitaries D_1, D_2 and permutation matrices P_1, P_2 if and only if there exist permutations P_1, P_2 with dephase(P_1*H*P_2) = H'. Equivalence of dephased 6x6 matrices is therefore decidable by an exact finite check over the 518400 permutation pairs, with no numerical invariant and no floating point.

Retained exact derivation, supplied by the repository owner and replayable but not yet machine-replayed. Under the idempotent Chinese Remainder relabelling of Z_6 the sixth-order discrete Fourier matrix satisfies F_6 = P*(F_2 tensor F_3')*Q for permutation matrices P and Q, where F_3' is F_3 with columns permuted by the map d -> 2*d mod 3. Since C^2 admits three pairwise mutually unbiased bases and C^3 admits four, the tensor lemma yields three pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^6 whose first member is the standard basis and whose second is equivalent to the Fourier basis; row relabelling is a global permutation unitary that fixes the standard basis as a set and column relabelling reorders vectors within one basis, so neither changes the unordered pair. Hence the pair consisting of the standard basis and the Fourier basis EXTENDS to a triple, at least three pairwise mutually unbiased bases exist in C^6, and every pair equivalent to the standard-basis-with-F_2-tensor-F_3 pair is extendible and therefore worthless as an unextendibility target. The entries of the third basis lie in mu_12, which is why the coefficient field is Q(zeta_12) and not Q(zeta_6).

Every quantity on a trust path is an exact element of Q(zeta_12) or an exact rational, represented as integer or rational coefficient vectors reduced by Phi_12. Unbiasedness is decided as an exact equality of algebraic integers using the integral norm form rather than any square root. No tolerance, residual, or floating-point number exists on the trust path, and a certificate containing one is discarded rather than rounded.

Failure of a numerical search, a floating-point semidefinite bound, an interval computation with floating endpoints, or an optimizer reporting no solution never certifies nonexistence of a quadruple or unextendibility of any pair. The repository owner rejects floating-point solvers outright and ADR-0035 admits no solver and records that no interval or residual-reconstruction path exists. Such output is exploration-only, must be labelled as such, and must never be replayed as a bound. Reports of published numerical evidence are subject to the same rule regardless of source.

Because a triple of pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^6 exists, the route of proving that NO pair extends to a triple is already refuted and must not be attempted. Unextendibility of one particular pair excludes exactly the quadruples containing that pair and nothing else, so it is a partial exclusion and never a resolution of the frozen statement. The frozen statement is equivalent to the assertion that no triple extends to a quadruple, and only an argument covering all triples, or a complete exclusion covering all quadruples, can settle it. A single-pair certificate must never be reported as resolving Problem 10.2, as resolving any family, or as saying anything about pairs other than the certified one.

A pair chosen as a bounded-slice waypoint must be certified NOT equivalent to the standard-basis-with-F_2-tensor-F_3 pair before any unextendibility search runs on it, using the exact finite dephasing check rather than a recalled claim of inequivalence. Adopting a tensor-equivalent pair guarantees a wasted slice, because such a pair is provably extendible. A pair whose inequivalence cannot be certified exactly must not be adopted, and in that case acquisition of the review becomes the gating step rather than a convenience.

The planning notes report that McNulty and Weigert's 2026 review contains Problem 10.2, the headline conjecture that no four mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension 6, and Problem 10.6, the stepping stone asking that a given pair be shown non-extendible to a triple or quadruple; that the review lists pair families named M_6^(1), K_6^(2), and K_6^(3); and that strong published numerical evidence of unextendibility exists for some parameter values. The review is not acquired. The exact problem statements, the family names, their parametrizations, and whether any listed member is tensor-inequivalent are all unverified. The ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check must cover every one of these.

formalization.statement: not ( exists B1 B2 B3 B4 : orthonormal_basis(C^6), forall s t in {1,2,3,4}, s != t -> (forall a b in {0..5}, abs2(inner(B_s[a], B_t[b])) = 1/6) ); equivalently forall B1 B2 B3 B4 : orthonormal_basis(C^6), exists s t in {1,2,3,4} with s != t, exists a b in {0..5}, abs2(inner(B_s[a], B_t[b])) != 1/6
quantifiers: forall B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4 orthonormal bases of C^6, with no quotient applied to the frozen statement
exists s, t in {1,2,3,4} with s != t, naming a pair that fails to be unbiased
exists a, b in {0,...,5}, naming the failing pair of basis vectors
in the negated existential form: not exists a set of four pairwise mutually unbiased bases, all six pairs and all 36 conditions per pair required

quantifier_mapping: no four mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension 6
forall four orthonormal bases of C^6, some pair among them is not mutually unbiased
an unordered set of four, required to be pairwise unbiased, so all six pairs are constrained
the indices of the unbiasedness conditions
forall a, b in {0,...,5}, all 36 conditions per pair, none omitted
not quantified in the frozen statement at all; it acts on candidate quadruples and is used only to normalize the search
a given pair, in the stepping-stone Problem 10.6
not the frozen target; it appears only as a bounded-slice waypoint whose resolution excludes the quadruples containing that pair
definition_mapping: squared modulus of every cross inner product equals exactly 1/6
four orthonormal bases, pairwise unbiased; a star configuration around one fixed basis is a rejected reading
the complex space C^6 with the standard Hermitian inner product; no other composite dimension is in scope
Q(zeta_12), degree 4 over Q, minimal polynomial x^4 - x^2 + 1; needed because a tensor-constructed basis of C^6 has entries in mu_12
the factor 1/6 carried as an exact rational scalar; sqrt(6) never represented

a replayable exact identity over Q(zeta_12): a Nullstellensatz cofactor representation of 1, a rational sum-of-squares Positivstellensatz identity, or a complete exact interval-exclusion cover with rational endpoints
the maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in C^6
not the frozen statement, but related to it: the retained derivation fixes the lower bound at three, so the frozen statement is equivalent to that maximum being exactly three
assumption_delta: The target is escalated from a single frozen pair to the headline conjecture Problem 10.2 on operator instruction, so the frozen claim is a universal nonexistence rather than a statement about one object, and target_claim.scope moves from particular to unrestricted_universal.

The equivalence group is removed from the frozen statement and retained only as a search normalization, because a universal nonexistence needs no quotient; its soundness as a normalization is recorded as a definitional assumption instead.

The previously frozen pair, the standard basis with the sixth-order Fourier basis, is refuted as an unextendibility target by a retained exact derivation and is now recorded as a finding rather than a target.
Consequently the route of proving that no pair extends to a triple is refused outright, and the frozen statement is restated as the assertion that no triple extends to a quadruple.
The or-quadruple disjunct that appeared in the stepping-stone problem is absorbed: quadruples are now the subject of the frozen statement rather than an alternative to triples.

The bounded slice can no longer claim to attack the frozen statement directly; it is explicitly a waypoint programme, and its waypoint pair must be certified tensor-inequivalent or acquisition becomes the gating step.
edge_case_delta: Unbiasedness of a dephased basis to the standard basis is automatic once every entry of its matrix has modulus 1, so 36 conditions per such pair collapse to a modulus condition.
Zero is not a permitted entry of a complex Hadamard matrix; every entry has modulus exactly 1, so no degenerate column can satisfy the conditions vacuously.

A quadruple is a set, so reordering the four bases or reordering and rephasing the vectors inside any of them gives the same solution; counts are meaningful only modulo the frozen group, which excludes conjugation and basis role permutation.
A star configuration in which three bases are each unbiased to one fixed basis is generally easier to satisfy than a pairwise quadruple and does not witness the negation of the frozen statement.

The retained derivation shows the negation cannot be approached by pair unextendibility alone: since a triple exists, at least one pair in C^6 is extendible, so any universal-over-pairs route is already refuted.
If the exact stabilizer of a waypoint pair turns out larger than expected, the search space shrinks without losing solutions, because the stabilizer is computed rather than assumed.

success_criteria: an explicit set of four pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^6 with exact algebraic entries, every one of the six pairs and all 36 conditions per pair verified, refuting the frozen conjecture
an exact nonexistence certificate for four pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^6, replayed as a polynomial identity by an independent verifier

or an explicit unresolved outcome recording the replayed triple that fixes the lower bound at three, the certified exclusion set of pairs whose containing quadruples are ruled out, the exhausted root-of-unity envelope, and the smallest remaining obligation
stopping_rules: stop on an explicit set of four pairwise mutually unbiased bases of C^6 whose every exact condition is verified
stop on an exact nonexistence certificate replayed as a polynomial identity by an independent verifier
stop when fresh model spend reaches USD 20
stop when two consecutive review points close no obligation, certify no newly excluded pair, and widen no envelope
never promote unextendibility of one pair, exhaustion of a root-of-unity envelope, or failure of any search to the nonexistence of four mutually unbiased bases
abandon the clique or equivalence-class search and record the frontier when the frozen node budget is reached
discard rather than round any floating-point value that reaches a certificate
